messages:
alex chan: Heads up — after the kernel-selector tweak landed in canary, p50 for our small-prompt suite is up ~8%. Running traces now and will drop summaries here.

maria gonzalez: which traces are you running? full nsys or quick perf sampling? profiler overhead matters for safe-prod.

daniel fletcher: did a quick nsys on canary-2 with skewed batch distribution (lots of batch_size=1). NVTX timeline shows a KV-cache stall right before the first kernel dispatch, then fallback to generic_gemm for a bunch of steps.

perf-bot: nsys run summary (canary-2): total wall 118.6s, profiler overhead ~11.9% vs baseline run. Kernel time split: generic_gemm ~49%, attn_cuda ~31%, memcpy/overhead ~20%. Full timeline saved to s3://perf/canary-2/1825004321/nsys.qdrep

alex chan: 12% is too high to enable broadly in prod. We need guardrails for safe-production profiling: sampling rate, host subset, and automatic kill-switch.

priya rao: I prototyped a hybrid probe: sample 1/1000 requests for full nsys traces but run a micro-timeline (low overhead counters) on 1% of requests. If the micro-timeline detects a suspicious pattern (KV-miss streak > 50 or kernel switchbacks > 3 within 200ms), escalate and run full capture for that request. Staging numbers look promising.

maria gonzalez: paste the nsys command you used? also we should discuss what micro counters we expose (kv-hit/hit-distance, kernel-choice histograms).

priya rao: code block:
```
# quick nsys capture for canary-2
nsys profile --output /tmp/canary-2-1825004321 --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi:start,stop \
  --sample=none --force-overwrite --stop-on-exit --sleep-before=0 --capture-children true \
  -- ./deploy/canary_run.sh --workload small-prompts
```
The micro-timeline is just a tiny eBPF + lightweight NVTX wrapper that emits counters to our metrics sink (no full stacks). Overhead ~0.5-1% on GPU.

daniel fletcher: note from my runs: pure sampling (perf) dropped overhead to ~2-3% but it completely misses the small-ordering issues that cause the runtime to pick the wrong kernel. Sampling gives good hotspots but not scheduling/order details. Hybrid seems necessary.

alex chan: proposed guardrails (candidate):
- Full nsys traces only on canary hosts and a tiny sample (0.1% of requests).
- Micro-timeline on 1% of requests clusterwide (always on).
- Trigger rules: if micro-timeline sees KV-cache miss streak > 50 OR kernel-switchbacks > 3 OR latency delta > p90+20%, escalate and collect full trace for that request.
- Global stop: if observed profiler overhead per-host > 8% for 5min or GPU util > 85%, auto-disable profiling on that host.
- Data retention: rotate/expire traces after 14d and scrub tokens/keys.

maria gonzalez: +1. add a hard upper bound on profiling concurrency per host (eg max 2 full traces simultaneously) and require opt-in for any CPU-side instrumentation that alters scheduler affinity. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created PR https://git.internal/redwood/perf-configs/pull/427 with sampling policy, micro-probe wiring, and initial trigger rules. CI runs pending.

priya rao: I'll kick off a guarded canary tonight at 02:00 PST with these rules. tagging @daniel fletcher to watch KV counters and kernel-choice logs.

daniel fletcher: watching. if we see kernel-selection flips correlated with increased small-batch traffic, we'll flip the selector back to old heuristic and file a follow-up perf-regression ticket. :eyes:

alex chan: great. after the run, drop a short thread with the delta table (p50/p90/p99, overhead, sample counts) and any interesting nvtx screenshots. also add an escalation playbook for perf-bot alerts so oncall knows what to do.

maria gonzalez: will do. thanks team — this hybrid approach should give us the ordering detail we need without burning prod.

perf-bot: monitoring rule added: profile-overhead-host > 8% for 5m -> alert #oncall-perf
